story.head: Stay out of the box, Islanders
paras: The Islanders (10-6-5) lost 4-3 in overtime to Winnipeg on Thursday, and the Red Wings (8-11-3) lost 4-1 to Boston on Wednesday. Going in, the Islanders are fourth in the Metropolitan (tied for 15th in the NHL) and the Wings seventh in the Atlantic (tied for 26th).

The Islanders’ record (.595) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.492), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Red Wings have played better than their record (.432) says: their chances are worth about .542, and their finishing has held them back. If their records matched their chances, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.
This season, the Red Wings have been outscored 66-56, but only 41-37 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 20-11.

The Islanders roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (1st). They also get their defensemen shooting (1st), so their defensemen shoot a lot, and the Red Wings’ not so much. The Red Wings block more shots than almost anyone (2nd) and take away shots from the point (4th lowest), but ice the puck a lot (30th). The Red Wings’ power play (6th) could do real damage against the Islanders’ penalty kill (29th), though their penalty killers create chances of their own going the other way.

Matthew Schaefer (9 G / 15 A / 24 P in 21 GP) leads the Islanders in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Bo Horvat (9 G / 12 A / 21 P in 21 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Red Wings, Lucas Raymond (9 G / 13 A / 22 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Alex DeBrincat (7 G / 9 A / 16 P in 22 GP) is next in line.

Ilya Sorokin (8-4-2 / .918 SV% in 14 GS) has been a rock in net for the Islanders and is expected to start. John Gibson (4-7-1 / .862 SV% in 13 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Detroit, but is expected to start.
